title: AHB Assertion Library: Trigger, Obligation, Exception
description: Open each checker to see the precise antecedent, required behavior, protocol exception, and DV failure signature that prevent false assertions.

signals.name: Accepted wait-state stability
signals.description: When NONSEQ or SEQ address/control is pending and HREADY is LOW, the master holds that accepted transfer information until completion.
signals.sampled: Rising HCLK edges while the valid transfer remains pending
values: Stable HWDATA for a stalled write data phase
signals.verificationNote: Do not write a blanket $stable assertion for every low-HREADY cycle: IDLE/BUSY transitions and the first ERROR cycle have specification-defined exceptions.

signals.name: Transfer-type legality
signals.description: A burst begins with NONSEQ and continuing data beats use SEQ. BUSY preserves an intended continuation without creating a transfer.
values: INCR may terminate after BUSY with IDLE or NONSEQ
SINGLE cannot be followed by BUSY
signals.verificationNote: An undefined-length INCR may terminate after BUSY with IDLE or NONSEQ. A simple BUSY→IDLE ban will produce false failures.

signals.name: Address progression
signals.description: For each accepted SEQ beat, predict the next address from HSIZE and HBURST, including the wrap boundary and the 1 KB limit.
signals.verificationNote: Do not advance the predictor on BUSY, IDLE, or a waited cycle.

signals.name: Two-cycle ERROR
signals.description: Once the first ERROR cycle occurs with HRESP=1 and HREADYOUT=0, the next cycle completes with HRESP=1 and HREADYOUT=1.
signals.sampled: Consecutive HCLK cycles in the response data phase
signals.verificationNote: Additional wait states may precede ERROR1 only with HRESP=OKAY. Do not trigger the property from ERROR2 as though it were a new response.

signals.name: IDLE and BUSY response
signals.description: Slaves provide a zero-wait OKAY response to IDLE and BUSY transfer types and ignore them as data transfers.
signals.sampled: When HTRANS is IDLE or BUSY
signals.verificationNote: Also assert that no write side effect or transaction count increment occurs for these transfer types.

signals.name: Exclusive response legality
signals.description: When Exclusive_Transfers is supported, HEXOKAY can only be asserted when HREADY is asserted and must not be asserted in the same cycle as HRESP.
signals.verificationNote: Gate the assertion by the interface capability and the accepted exclusive transfer context; HEXOKAY=0 is not itself an ERROR.

signals.name: Bounded service contract
signals.description: A project can require completion or grant within a configured bound, but the AHB protocol does not choose an arbitration fairness policy or one universal maximum wait count.
signals.verificationNote: Document the bound and its assumptions. A fixed-priority arbiter cannot satisfy unconditional fairness under a permanently requesting higher-priority master.
